jobs.title: Senior Data Analyst – Customer Data Platforms (CDP)
jobs.description:
Compensation & Location

Location:
Torrance, CA
Pay Range:
$54.00 – $61.00 per hour (based on experience and internal equity)
Schedule:
Full-time, contract; long-term opportunity
Work Type:
4 days/week on site; 1 day/week remote
Benefits:
Health, Vision, Dental, Life Insurance, 401k, Continuing and on-demand education

📍 Must be willing to work onsite in Torrance, CA (LA County)

‼️ ONLY W2 – NO CORP to CORP – NO 3rd Parties

✅ Sponsorship is available for this role

Position Summary

We are seeking a Senior Data Analyst / CDP Developer
to support enterprise Customer Data Platform (CDP) operations, improve data quality, and deliver scalable data solutions across large customer and event datasets. This role blends advanced SQL development, CDP integration, workflow orchestration, and production data troubleshooting.

The ideal candidate brings strong expertise in customer data platforms, advanced SQL engineering, Python automation, and cloud data environments
, along with experience supporting production data pipelines and customer data privacy requirements.

Key Responsibilities

Data Analysis & Development

Analyze customer data, event streams, and large-scale datasets to generate insights
Develop and optimize advanced SQL queries across Presto, Hive, and NoSQL environments
Use Python for data processing, automation, API integrations, and workflow support
Perform exploratory data analysis and anomaly detection
Document data processes, business rules, and workflows

CDP & Pipeline Operations

Support CDP workflow orchestration (Digdag, TD Workflows, or similar tools)
Monitor and enhance data quality frameworks and observability pipelines
Maintain CI/CD and Git-based version control for data code and documentation
Support end-to-end data lifecycle from ingestion to activation

Troubleshooting & Production Support

Diagnose data pipeline failures and workflow issues
Perform root cause analysis using logs and monitoring tools
Support production job monitoring, data validation, and output verification
Implement fixes and reliability improvements

Data Governance & Compliance

Ensure adherence to privacy and compliance standards (GDPR, CCPA, PII handling)
Support identity resolution, schema design, and profile unification

What You’ll Be Working On

Customer Data Platform integrations and pipeline operations
Large-scale customer and event data processing
Data quality, automation, and workflow optimization
Cross-functional data solutions supporting CRM, marketing, and analytics teams

Required Skills & Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Data Science, Computer Science, Engineering, or related field
8+ years combined experience in data analysis, data engineering, or data operations
Advanced SQL development and query optimization (Presto, Hive, NoSQL environments)
Experience working with Customer Data Platforms and CRM data integrations
Strong Python experience for data automation and APIs
Cloud data platform familiarity (AWS preferred)
Experience with workflow orchestration tools (Digdag, TD Workflows, or similar)
Experience supporting production data environments
Experience with data quality frameworks, monitoring, and alerting
Strong communication and cross-functional collaboration skills

Preferred Skills

Experience with Treasure Data CDP or similar platforms (Informatica, Adobe, Salesforce CDP, Tealium, mParticle)
Experience with data modeling, identity resolution, and profile unification
Experience with CI/CD and Git-based workflows
Strong privacy and compliance experience (GDPR, CCPA, PII handling)
3+ years of Big 4 consulting experience (preferred)
Stable work history within large enterprise organizations

jobs.title: Research Program Coordinator
jobs.description:
Overview

Please note that this position is contingent upon the successful award of a contract currently under bid.

Goldbelt Apex, a part of the Healthcare Technology Transformation Group, is a data-focused company dedicated to process and quality in every aspect. As experts in healthcare IT experts, Apex is committed to building systems for healthcare organizations to seamlessly communicate and exchange data across different systems and devices.

Summary

The Research Program Coordinator supports planning, execution, coordination, tracking, and administration of hearing research studies, public health initiatives, regulatory activities, and stakeholder engagement efforts supporting military hearing health programs.

Work location: Remote or Hybrid in Maryland

Responsibilities

Essential Job Functions:

Coordinate research and public health projects.
Maintain schedules, milestones, and action-item tracking.
Support IRB submissions and regulatory compliance activities.
Coordinate stakeholder meetings and communications.
Support participant recruitment and study logistics.
Maintain project documentation and records.
Assist with preparation of reports, presentations, and briefings.
Monitor deliverables and contract performance requirements.
Support workforce planning and resource coordination.
Assist with quality control and continuous improvement activities.

Qualifications

Necessary Skills and Knowledge:

Possess excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Possess knowledge of Microsoft Office applications.
Possess excellent ability to manage multiple tasks with competing deadlines.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree
Minimum two (2) years of project coordination experience
U.S. Citizenship required.
Ability to obtain and maintain a favorable Government suitability determination.
Ability to obtain and maintain SECRET clearance if required.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience supporting federal healthcare, public health, or research programs.
Experience supporting clinical research studies and human-subjects research.
Experience coordinating IRB documentation and submissions.
Experience supporting military medical treatment facilities.
Familiarity with hearing conservation, occupational health, or readiness programs.
PMP, CAPM, or equivalent project management certification.
Experience supporting geographically dispersed teams, hybrid work environments, remote operations, or nationwide field activities.
Preferred candidates will have current or prior experience supporting the Defense Health Agency (DHA), Hearing Center of Excellence (HCE), National Military Audiology and Speech Pathology Center (NMASC), Defense Centers for Public Health (DCPH), Military Health System (MHS), Veterans Health Administration (VHA), military treatment facilities (MTFs), hearing conservation programs, auditory readiness initiatives, or other military health and public health programs.

Pay And Benefits

The salary range for this position is $75,000.00 to $95,000.00 annually.

At Goldbelt, we value and reward our team's dedication and hard work. We provide a competitive base salary commensurate with your qualifications and experience. As an employee, you'll enjoy a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, and vision insurance, a 401(k) plan with company matching, tax-deferred savings options, supplementary benefits, paid time off, and professional development opportunities.

Specialized Programs Coordinator

Salary: Per NC DPI Salary Schedule

Position:
Specialized Programs Coordinator

Reports To:
Director of Exceptional Children

Position Status:
12-Month, Full-Time

Department:
Exceptional Children

Position Summary

The Specialized Programs Coordinator provides district-level leadership, coordination, supervision, and support for specialized programs and services that address the unique educational, communication, physical, sensory, nutritional, technological, and access needs of students with disabilities. The coordinator oversees assigned specialized staff and programs, collaborates with schools and district departments, supports compliance and program quality, and provides professional development and technical assistance to staff.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Specialized Program Leadership

Provide leadership and coordination for specialized programs and services across the district.
Oversee assigned specialized staff and services, including Visual Impairment (VI), Deaf/Hard of Hearing (DHH), educational interpreters, Adapted Physical Education, music therapy, assistive technology, and other specialized programs.
Monitor program implementation and service delivery and make recommendations for improvement.
Collaborate with school administrators, EC staff, families, related service providers, and district departments to address student needs.
Assist with staffing, budgeting, purchasing, resource allocation, and program planning related to specialized services.

Specialized Services

Coordinate VI and DHH services and support staff serving students with sensory disabilities.
Coordinate educational interpreter services and communication supports.
Oversee specialized meal-time programs in collaboration with School Nutrition Services, schools, families, and appropriate staff to address feeding, positioning, safety, and other unique student needs.
Coordinate special transportation needs in collaboration with the Transportation Department, including facilitating monthly coordination meetings to address student needs, concerns, equipment, safety, and service delivery.
Provide leadership and support for Adapted Physical Education and music therapy programs and staff.
Coordinate assistive technology and specialized equipment, including acquisition, implementation, inventory, maintenance, and staff training.
Serve as a district resource for schools regarding specialized equipment, accommodations, accessibility, and student supports.

Professional Development and Technical Assistance

Develop and provide professional development for teachers, teacher assistants, administrators, related service providers, specialized staff, and other school personnel.
Provide training and technical assistance related to VI, DHH, interpreting, specialized meal-time programs, transportation, adapted physical education, music therapy, assistive technology, specialized equipment, accessibility, accommodations, and inclusive practices.
Provide ongoing consultation, coaching, and problem-solving support to school-based staff.
Identify professional development needs and coordinate training based on student needs, staff needs, compliance requirements, and best practices.

Compliance and Program Monitoring

Support compliance with federal, state, and local requirements related to specialized programs and services.
Monitor services and programs for alignment with student IEPs, district procedures, and applicable regulations.
Maintain appropriate documentation and records related to specialized programs, staffing, equipment, and professional development.
Assist the Director of Exceptional Children with program evaluation, reporting, audits, and compliance activities.
Stay current with laws, regulations, research, and best practices related to specialized programming.

Collaboration and Communication

Serve as a liaison between the Exceptional Children Department, schools, families, and district departments regarding specialized programs and student needs.
Establish effective working relationships with school and district personnel to ensure coordinated services and supports.
Participate in meetings, planning activities, and district initiatives related to specialized programming, accessibility, inclusion, and student safety.
Assist the Director of Exceptional Children with special projects and other responsibilities as assigned.

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Knowledge of special education and the educational needs of students with disabilities.
Knowledge of specialized programs, assistive technology, adaptive equipment, accessibility, and accommodations.
Strong organizational, communication, collaboration, leadership, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to coordinate multiple programs, personnel, and projects across multiple school sites.
Ability to provide effective professional development, coaching, and technical assistance.
Ability to collaborate effectively across departments and with school personnel, families, and community partners.
Commitment to equitable access, inclusion, and high-quality educational opportunities for students with disabilities.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Special Education, Exceptional Children, Education, or a related field from an accredited college or university.
Appropriate North Carolina licensure/certification as required by the position.
Demonstrated experience working with students with disabilities and specialized programs.
Demonstrated leadership, supervisory, or program coordination experience.
Experience providing professional development, training, consultation, or technical assistance to school staff.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree in Special Education, Exceptional Children, Educational Leadership, or a related field.
Experience coordinating district-wide specialized programs or related services.
Experience with VI, DHH, assistive technology, specialized equipment, or other specialized student services.

Work Schedule

This is a 12-month, full-time district-level position
requiring flexibility to visit schools, attend meetings, provide professional development, and respond to specialized program needs throughout the year.

Supervisory Relationship

The Specialized Programs Coordinator reports directly to the Director of Exceptional Children
and provides leadership, coordination, and supervision of assigned specialized program staff and services.

Seniority level Mid-Senior level
Employment type Full-time
Job function Other
Industries Primary and Secondary Education
